/ S.374(2) CR.P.C PRAYING TO  SET ASIDE THE ORDER DATED 31.08.2012 PASSED BY THE  P.O., FTC-IV, BANGALORE IN S.C.No.1330/2010 - CONVICTING  THE APPELLANT/ACCUSED-1 FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 498A  -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:6213  CRL.A No. 991 of 2012 AND 304B OF IPC AND ALSO U/S 3 & 4 OF D.P.ACT, 1961 AND ETC.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR DICTATING JUDGMENT THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

This appeal is filed by appellant - accused No. 1 praying to set aside the judgment of conviction dated 31.08.2012 and order of sentence dated 01.09.2012 passed in S.C. No. 1330/2010 by the Presiding Officer, Fast Track Court, Bengaluru.
Appellant - accused No. 1 has been convicted for offence under Section 498-A, 304- B of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (hereinafter referred to as `D.P. Act').

2. The appellant - accused No. 1 has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 10 years and to pay fine of Rs.25,000/- for offence under Section 304-B of IPC; he is further sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 5 years and to pay fine of Rs.20,000/-
for offence under Section 3 of NC: 2024:KHC:6213 the D.P. Act and further sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of one year and to pay fine of Rs.2,000/- for offence under Section 4 of the D.P. Act.
The trial Court has ordered all the sentences to run concurrently.
The trial Court has not passed separate sentence for offence under Section 498-A of IPC.

3. Factual matrix of the prosecution case is that the marriage of appellant - accused No. 1 was solemnized with Smt. Srilakshmi (deceased), daughter of P.W.1, three years prior to 22.04.2010 at Gunthakal of Ananthapur district, Andhra Pradesh.
Appellant - accused No. 1 and his wife, after marriage, lived together for some time at Gunthakal and Hyderabad.

At the time of marriage amount of Rs.2,60,000/- in cash, 20 gms gold chain, 2 gold rings were given to appellant - accused No. 1 as dowry apart from giving 14 tholas of gold ornaments to Smt. Srilakshmi by her parents.

Appellant - accused No. 1 and his wife - deceased Srilakshmi, six months prior to the incident, came over to Bengaluru and were residing NC: 2024:KHC:6213 together with accused Nos. 2 and 3 in a house at Chunchakatta, Bengaluru.
The accused persons subjected Srilakshmi to physical and mental cruelty, harassed her and demanded her to bring further dowry from her parents' house.

The deceased Srilakshmi declined to bring further dowry from her parents' house as demanded by the accused persons, so, the accused persons did not provide her food properly and also not provided medical treatment to her though she was suffering from sickness.
Appellant - accused No. 1 took the Suresh Babu vs The State Of Karnataka By on 14 February, 2024

deceased Srilakshmi to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru on 22.04.2010 at about 06.30 am and the Doctors therein, on examination, declared that she had died on the way to the hospital.
Charge sheet has been filed against appellant - accused No. 1 and accused Nos.2 and 3 for offence under Sections 498-A, 304 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of D.P. Act.

On committal of the case,
the Sessions Judge has framed charges for the aforesaid offences.
In order to prove the charge the prosecution examined P.W.1 to P.W.15 and got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.28.
The prosecution has recorded NC: 2024:KHC:6213 the statement of the accused under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
The accused persons examined one Dr. Pradeep as their witness as D.W.1 and got marked Ex.D.1 to Ex.D.4.

The trial Court after hearing arguments on both sides formulated points for consideration and after appreciating the evidence on record convicted appellant - accused No. 1 as noted above and acquitted accused Nos.2 and 3.
Said judgment of conviction and order of sentence has been challenged in this appeal.

4. Heard learned counsel for appellant - accused No. 1 and learned HCGP for respondent - State.
5.
Learned counsel for appellant - accused No. 1 would contend that there is no allegation of demand of dowry or harassment to the deceased by the accused persons in the complaint -
Ex . P.1

. Death of the deceased is due to septicemia as a result of cellulites of right leg as opined by the Doctor who conducted postmortem examination over the dead body of the deceased and gave postmortem report as per Ex.P.20.
Therefore, the death of NC: 2024:KHC:6213 the deceased is natural death and provisions of Section 304-B of IPC is not attracted.
He contends that appellant - accused No. 1 was not present at the engagement ceremony and he has not received any dowry.
P.W.1 - father of the deceased has not stated when he gave dowry.
The deceased and appellant - accused No. 1 were residing at Bengaluru at the time of death of the deceased after shifting from Hyderabad 6 months prior to the incident.
Appellant - accused No. 1 and the deceased were not in contact with P.W.1 and his family members as admitted by P.W.1.
Evidence of P.W.1 to P.W.3 is improvement from their version in their statement and the same can be seen in their cross-examination.
Evidence of P.W.1 to P.W.5 does not establish that the deceased was harassed and ill-treated 6 months prior to her death.
He contends that the deceased died natural death and the injuries which are said to have been found on her body and which are noted in the postmortem report are not the cause for the death.

The neighbours who are examined as P.W.11 to P.W.13 have not supported the case of the NC:
2024:KHC:6213 prosecution and there is no evidence to establish that the accused persons harassed and ill-treated the deceased in Bengaluru immediately prior to her death.
Even payment of dowry at the time of marriage is an after thought as it is not stated in the complaint - Ex.P.1.
He placed reliance on the following decisions.
I. Raman Kumar Vs. State of Punjab, 2009 (16) SCC II.

On these grounds he has sought for dismissal of the appeal.
7. On the grounds made out and considering the arguments advanced the following point arises for my consideration.
" Whether the trial Court erred in convicting the appellant - accused No. 1 for offence under Section 498-A, 304-B of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of D.P. Act?
8. My answer to the above point is in the affirmative for the following reasons.
Date of marriage of appellant - accused No. 1 with the deceased is 05.05.2007 and date of death of the deceased is 22.04.2010.
The appellant - accused No.1 took his wife - deceased Srilakshmi to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru on 22.04.2010 and the Doctor who examined her opined that she died on the way to the hospital.
NC: 2024:KHC:6213 Ex.P.28 is the death memo issued by the Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru dated 22.04.2010.
P.W.8 is the Doctor who conducted postmortem examination over the dead body of the deceased and gave report as per Ex.P.20.The
Doctor opined that death is due to septicemia as a result of cellulites of right leg.

He has also stated that he found 6 injuries on the dead body of the deceased and they are noted in the postmortem report - Ex.P.20 and opined that those injuries might have been caused one week prior to her death.
In the cross-examination the Doctor has stated that the said 6 injuries found on the body of the deceased are simple injuries.
It is not the opinion of the Doctor that the said 6 injuries have caused the death of the deceased.
The Doctor has stated that the dead body of the deceased was very lean and bones were visible on her body.
The Doctor also found bedsores measuring 7 CM X 6 CM present on the backside of her body.
The Doctor also found that there was injection given mark on the left wrist.
It is accusation of the prosecution that the deceased was not given proper food and medical treatment.
The very - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:6213 injection mark on the left wrist itself shows that she was given medical treatment.
The Doctor in his cross- examination has stated that the said injection mark is 1 or 2 days old.
9. The accused have examined D.W.1 who is the pathologist working in Kanishka Diagnostics and Research Centre, Bengaluru.

sentences.text: He has produced Ex.D.2 and stated that it is the blood test report issued by him and he has taken blood sample of the deceased on 10.03.2010 and examined it.
He has further stated that chest X-Ray of the deceased was taken on 10.03.2010 by Dr. Sachidesh K and his report is at Ex.D.3.
Ex.D.4 is the certificate issued by D.W.1.
In the cross-examination D.W.1 has stated that he cannot say how was the health condition of the deceased Srilakshmi.

Said documents,
evidence of D.W.1 and injection mark noted in the postmortem report will indicate that medical treatment was provided to the deceased.

Considering all these aspects it is clear that the death of the Suresh Babu vs The State Of Karnataka By on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5845286/
4 deceased is not unnatural death.

- 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:6213 10. Section 304-B of IPC reads thus:
304B.
Dowry death.

- (1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called "dowry death",
and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death.
(2) Whoever commits dowry death shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life."

One of the essential ingredients to attract offence of dowry death under Section 304-B of IPC is that the death of woman has to be occurred otherwise than under normal circumstances within 7 years of her marriage.

Even though the death of the deceased, in the instant case, is within 7 - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:6213 years of her marriage, it cannot be said that death occurred other than under normal circumstances in view of the opinion of the Doctor who conducted postmortem examination over the dead body of the deceased.
Death of the deceased has not been caused by burns or bodily injury.

The other aspect that deceased was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for or in connection with non-payment of dowry is required to be ascertained from the evidence on record.
11. P.W.1 is the father of the deceased.
He, on coming to know about the death of the deceased, came to Bengaluru and saw the dead body in the hospital and thereafter filed complaint as per Ex.P.1.

In Ex.P.1 it is stated that the deceased who is his daughter and appellant - accused No. 1 who is his son-in-law after marriage lived happily for some time and thereafter his daughter was harassed physically and mentally by the accused.
It is not alleged that the said physical and mental harassment was due to non-payment of dowry.

It is - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:6213 further stated in the complaint - Ex.P.1 that the deceased and her husband shifted from Hyderabad to Bengaluru and thereafter since 6 months his daughter and son-in-law did not contact them.

Said aspect itself goes to show that P.W.1 - father of the deceased was not Suresh Babu vs The State Of Karnataka By on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5845286/
5 aware or not informed how the deceased was treated by her husband and his family members 6 months prior to her death.

sentences.text: P.W.1 even in his chief examination has stated that how the accused persons treated his daughter in Bengaluru has not been informed to him.

12. P.W.2 - the younger brother of the deceased has stated in his chief examination that 6 months prior to the death of the deceased the accused persons came with his elder sister to Bengaluru and he came to know the same through his relatives.
He has further stated that accused No. 2 who met him had not informed him about the deterioration of health of his sister - Srilakshmi.

13. P.W.3 - uncle of the deceased and younger brother of P.W.1 has stated that he came to know regarding the accused and deceased shifting from - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:6213 Hyderabad to Bengaluru, but, it was not intimated to him by the accused persons and his relatives told him that they are residing in first Cross, Annapoorneshwari Nagara,
Bengaluru.
14. P.W.4 is the mother of the deceased.
She has not stated regarding she meeting her daughter - Srilakshmi when she resided in Bengaluru 6 months prior to her death.
She only stated that she went to Hyderabad to see her daughter and accused persons did not allow her to enter the house and meet her daughter.
P.W.4 has stated that she was not able to meet her daughter - Srilakshmi when she resided in Bengaluru.
P.W.1 to P.W.4 have not stated that they had contact with the deceased over phone.
Said aspect itself goes to show that deceased was not in contact with P.W.1 to P.W.4, 6 months prior to her death when she resided along with her husband in Bengaluru.
Therefore, the evidence of P.W.1 to P.W.4 is not sufficient to show that accused persons ill-treated and assaulted the deceased prior to her death.
P.W.1 to P.W.5 have stated regarding payment of dowry in a sum of Rs.2,60,000/- in cash and 20 tholas of gold at the time of marriage.
Evidence of P.W.1 to P.W.5 does not establish that they gave dowry to appellant - accused No. 1 at the time of marriage.

P.W.1 immediately after the death of the deceased has filed complaint as per Ex.P.1 and it does not contain any allegation of giving dowry at the time of marriage and harassment of the deceased by the accused persons demanding dowry.
16. P.W.11 and P.W.13 are the neighbors of the house in which the accused and deceased resided at Bengaluru and P.W.12 is the landlord of the house in which the deceased and accused resided.
They have not stated anything with regard to appellant - accused No. 1 harassing the deceased, ill-treating her and demanding dowry.

Therefore, there is no evidence on record to establish that appellant - Suresh Babu vs The State Of Karnataka By on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5845286/
6 accused No. 1 harassed and ill- treated the deceased immediately prior to her death when he resided with her in Bengaluru.

sentences.text: Even the evidence on - 16 - NC: 2024:KHC:6213 record is not sufficient to hold that appellant - accused No. 1 has demanded and accepted dowry since he was not present at the time of engagement.

Therefore, the prosecution has not proved the guilt of appellant - accused No.1 beyond reasonable doubt and hence, benefit of doubt requires to be extended to appellant - accused No.
1.

Without considering all these aspects learned Sessions Judge has erred in convicting appellant - accused No. 1 for offence under Section 304-B and 498-A of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of D.P. Act.
17.

In the result, the following;
ORDER I.
The appeal is allowed.
II. The judgment of conviction dated 31.08.2012 and order of sentence dated 01.09.2012 passed in S.C. No. 1330/2010 by the Presiding Officer, Fast Track Court, Bengaluru is set aside.

III. Appellant - accused No.1 is acquitted for offence under Section 304-B and 498-A of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of D.P. Act.

In view of the above, I.A. No. 1/2024 seeking re-call of the order dated 18.01.2024 is allowed.
Issue intimation to the trial Court regarding recalling of the order dated 18.01.2024.
